newsitem.title: JAPAN: Petchem operations undisturbed by Tokyo oil spill.
newsitem.headline: Petchem operations undisturbed by Tokyo oil spill.

text.p: Operations at petrochemical firms located on the shore of Tokyo Bay have continued as normal despite a crude oil spill from a supertanker which scraped a reef in the bay on Wednesday morning, company spokesmen said.

"We put up oil fences around sea water intake pipes at the plant as a precaution, but otherwise everything has been running normally here," said a spokesman for Sumitomo Chemical Co Ltd. The company has its Anegasaki plant with an ethylene output capacity of 380,000 tonne per year on the bay.

Other firms with their plants on the shore of the bay, such as Maruzen Petrochemical Co Ltd and Mitsui Petrochemical Industries Ltd, said their plant operations, including loading and off-loading, have not been affected by the oil spill.
The 259,999 deadweight tonne Panamanian-flagged Diamond Grace was estimated to have spilled about 13,400 tonnes of crude oil, the Maritime Safety Agency said.
The supertanker was headed for Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd's Kawasaki refinery near Tokyo carrying 257,000 tonnes of crude oil at the time of the accident.
